chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from ʿIsa ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAli (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"When one of you performs istinja', let him use them [the stones] an odd number of times when water is not available."

key_terms.اَلْمَاءُ: water — its absence is the condition triggering permissibility of stone-wiping
key_terms.اِسْتَنْجَى: istinja' — ritual cleansing of private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.فَلْيُوتِرْ: let him make it odd — a jussive imperative expressing a legal obligation
key_terms.وَتْراً: witr — an odd number; the legally required count for stone-wiping

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of stones required for istinja' when water is not available?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a ruling of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) via Imam ʿAli (AS): when performing istinja' (ritual cleansing of private parts after relieving oneself) and water is unavailable, one must use an odd number of stones or pebbles. The requirement of an odd number (witr) is a foundational principle of istijmar (stone-wiping as a water substitute) in Shia fiqh. The ruling appears in the chapter on acts that necessitate ritual purification (taharah), establishing the minimum valid method of cleansing in the absence of water.
